name: A-thermal-field
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create an exceptionally art-directed HIGH-FIDELITY WEBSITE DESIGN CONCEPT for Cardinal Volta, an early-stage company turning industrial waste heat into electricity using Organic Rankine Cycle technology. This is design exploration, not a coded website. Produce a tall 2:3 image at high resolution, a polished continuous homepage design showing a desktop hero, a visually integrated scroll transition, and the beginning of a technology chapter. Each chapter spans the full canvas width. Straight-on flat UI, no device frame, no presentation background.

CONCEPT A: THERMAL FIELD. Museum-quality scientific visual identity: warm white, deep cardinal red, soft vermilion, pale peach light, graphite type. The core visual is a beautiful luminous volumetric thermal field, like fine interference contours and heat haze gradually gathering into a single controlled ribbon. The imagery must express dispersed heat becoming useful power, NOT an arbitrary object. No stock steel photograph, no factory hero, no metal sculpture, no donut, no floating turbine, no generic particle galaxy.

At top a quiet white header: text wordmark "Cardinal Volta" at left; navigation "Home   Technology   News   About   Contact" at right, all one consistent refined sans serif family. Large but exquisitely balanced left headline "A second life
for heat." at approximately 90px equivalent, regular medium grotesk, tight natural line spacing. Under it two readable lines "We turn industrial waste heat into electricity." One discreet red action "Explore our technology" with arrow. Typography is part of the composition with generous asymmetric whitespace; primary visual occupies right and lower hero, bleeding beyond page bounds. Thermal contours are broad, warm, atmospheric, translucent, visually rich and highly crafted; no clutter. Text remains sharply legible.

Moving downward, the same red thermal field expands horizontally across the entire website and the white background gradually becomes luminous coral then deep red, like a scroll-driven color transformation. The visual threads visibly gather. A large unnumbered statement "Energy worth recovering." sits in the transition, white on a clear part of the red field. This is a carefully composed change of atmosphere, not rectangular stacked unrelated blocks.

At bottom the red field narrows into a clean flowing line on a warm white background entering a minimal elegant process story with heading "Heat becomes power." Include four readable labels "Capture heat", "Generate power", "Cool", "Recirculate" integrated along one continuous fine path, not a dashboard of cards. A small readable sentence "Organic Rankine Cycle technology." All sizes hierarchy intentional. ONE sans serif family for both headings and small text, no monospace, no tiny uppercase numbered eyebrow text, no unnecessary labels. No fake logos, metrics, awards, device claims, fake data, news cards. Sophisticated transitions of color, cinematic gradients with soft film texture but crisp UI, outstanding whitespace, not a conventional split photo template. Entire page must look designed by an excellent independent climate-tech branding studio.
refinement: Refine this exact website concept mockup. Preserve the layout, all main typography, navigation, rich flowing thermal contours, colors, and technology story. Only remove the small decorative paragraph on the right of the central red section that reads 'Same heat. A brighter tomorrow.' and its short horizontal line. Restore the red thermal background seamlessly in that small area. Keep the large 'Energy worth recovering.' heading and everything else unchanged. Do not introduce any new text, labels, logos or graphical elements.

name: B-heat-into-current
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Generate a HIGH-FIDELITY art direction mockup of a premium climate technology website for "Cardinal Volta", waste heat into electricity. Tall 2:3 high resolution canvas showing a continuous desktop homepage: hero, flowing visual transition, and start of technology. Flat straight-on UI screenshot, no device frame or moodboard. This concept must be sophisticated, confident and cinematic.

CONCEPT B: HEAT INTO CURRENT. Palette: near-black aubergine / very dark oxblood, cardinal red, hot vermilion fading to luminous apricot and near-white. An expressive warm spectrum rather than black rectangular sections. One elegant modern humanist grotesk sans serif used in every size, generous readable body type. No monospace, no tiny numbered uppercase labels.

Top header integrated seamlessly into dark background: text wordmark "Cardinal Volta" warm white, slim legible links "Home   Technology   News   About   Contact". Hero headline monumental and beautifully spaced, located in the upper-left/center across wide negative space, exact text "Waste heat.
New power." in warm white. Beneath, smaller readable "Electricity from energy already there." with minimal outlined action "Discover how" and arrow. HERO VISUAL: across the lower half of hero a physically suggestive broad sheet of glowing turbulent thermal light, intricately layered but calm and intentional, curves and folds from left to right like rising hot air captured into direction. Organic soft bands rather than thin neon spaghetti; hazy hot interior and precise light boundary, extraordinary studio rendering. No metal objects, no turbine, no steel photograph, no stock energy globe.

The hot light blooms upward and outward through the MIDDLE TRANSITION, fills the full width with a stunning red-to-apricot-to-light gradient. Show the idea that scrolling brings the visitor through heat: the dark atmosphere smoothly opens into a luminous pale blush canvas. A single immense dark statement "Put wasted energy
to work." occupies this calm bright transition. Leave high-quality breathing room; no ornaments.

At BOTTOM, very pale neutral pink becomes white and the same ribbon resolves into a continuous thin cardinal-red path, entering an editorial technology chapter titled "A continuous cycle.
A new source of power." Three or four precise subtle vector-like process glyphs arranged in a spacious horizontal cycle, with legible plain labels "Heat in", "Conversion", "Electricity out" and a discreet return path. This is a conceptual explanatory visual, not an actual equipment rendering. The whole composition shares one persistent visual thread and has extraordinary continuity of color, typography and layout. No decorative pseudoengineering, fake numbers, fabricated product photography, cards, badges, all-caps microscopic labels or generic gradient blobs. This should feel like a memorable premium brand website, not a SaaS landing page.

name: C-see-the-invisible
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Design a premium WEBSITE CONCEPT IMAGE for "Cardinal Volta", a company recovering industrial waste heat to generate electricity. Tall 2:3 high resolution image, three connected moments of a desktop landing page: first impression, scroll transition, technology. Flat frontal full-width web UI, no laptop mockup, no design-board border. Design must be distinctly different from a conventional white split-photo landing page.

CONCEPT C: SEE THE INVISIBLE. Editorial industrial-science identity. Palette: icy light gray and white, deep navy-indigo, a controlled thermal spectrum from indigo through muted violet into cardinal red and luminous orange. ONE refined sans serif type family in ALL text, proportional not monospace. Boldest typography of the three: clean monumental uppercase used only for the main headline, with quiet sentence-case navigation and body.

Top white header with text wordmark "Cardinal Volta" in dark navy and small red square beside it, legible nav "Home   Technology   News   About   Contact". Very large dark navy main headline, exact text "THERE'S POWER
IN WHAT'S LEFT." set across most of the page width, remarkable optical spacing and line breaks. The hero features a custom ABSTRACT THERMAL IMAGING LANDSCAPE: beautifully rendered ghostlike transparent industrial pipe paths and heat exchange contours seen as a scientific heat-field image, largely indigo with a concentrated cardinal-red/orange hotspot. This is clearly stylized explanatory imagery, not a claimed real thermal scan or fabricated branded device. Place this full-bleed cinematic imaging plane BELOW and partially behind the lower headline, not as a stock photo in a right-side rectangle. Beneath headline readable short statement "We turn industrial waste heat into electricity." and simple dark action "Explore the technology". Excellent contrast.

In the middle transition, the imaging plane expands to the entire background. A wide vertical scanner-like band reveals warm hidden energy within the cool contours: left side cool subdued structure, center rich violet transition, right side vibrant thermal heat. The visual communicates revealing an overlooked resource. One large white statement "Make the invisible
valuable." with spacious composition, no technical legends, no invented temperature measurements, no meaningless small text. Color and image are deeply integrated rather than three cards.

Lower section: the image gradually dissolves into an ice-white background. A thin continuous red contour from the thermal image becomes the path of a minimal ORC cycle illustration with title "From heat to electricity." and legible labels "Evaporator", "Expander", "Condenser", "Pump", plus action "How it works". Keep process illustration understated and beautifully aligned, no product machine rendering. The transformation from industrial heat field to useful current must be visible in the art direction. No beige, no green sustainability cliché, no random metallic sculpture, no stock steel, no neon cyberpunk, no tiny uppercase eyebrow annotations, no fake logos, news, metrics, or awards. High visual intelligence, modern editorial typography and deliberate gradients, exquisite web design finish.
refinement: Targeted polish of this exact Cardinal Volta website mockup. Preserve main headline, navigation, large clear body text, buttons, cool industrial thermal visual, main composition and colors. Remove ALL four groups of decorative tiny uppercase microcopy and their decorative lines: top-right 'SAME INDUSTRY ...', left below hero 'HIDDEN ENERGY ...', bottom-left 'SAME ENERGY ...', bottom-right 'INDUSTRIAL HEAT ...'. Fill seamlessly with their existing backgrounds. Keep functional nav and actual diagram component labels. Correct the bottom technical schematic: Electricity out MUST branch from the Expander/generator at the top, NOT from the Condenser. Draw a distinct clean thin navy arrow from the expander toward the electricity lightning icon, and preserve a separate working-fluid loop from expander down to condenser, then pump, then evaporator. Remove any arrow that suggests the condenser generates electricity. In bottom left body text replace 'convert it into clean, usable electricity.' with 'convert it into usable electricity.' No new decorative microcopy. This is a simplified conceptual cycle illustration, not actual product equipment. All other portions unchanged.
